title: Prove a D-exponent (0,-1) owner index leaves the x1 residual
body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->

## Change and mathematical scope

Scoped proof. No new κ. The selected conditional value stays `781451/250000000` from the selected record (PR #6030). This does not change the selected frontier.

On the published two-edge feed, start from the sharp D-exponent-0 index of open PR #7033 and add arbitrary D-exponent-0 coefficients times `D3^{-1}` on the four final banks. Every such correction leaves x1 coefficient 1 on

```text
Q^{-1} C1 Q^2 C1 C3 D1 D3
```

because `D3^{-1}` moves every bank-x1 degree off `(1,1)` and a D-exponent-0 factor preserves degree. Keeping `x0 = D1 Q^{-1}` and y0 zero forces

```text
u1 = -u0 C1,  u2 = -u0 x,  u3 = 0,
```

with `x = Q^2 (I + Q) C1 Q` and `u0` an arbitrary D-exponent-0 element. The x1 column is then the residual plus `u0` times a fixed three-monomial defect. One bank forces `u0 = 0`. The four stored banks are only read.

Evidence class: a proof in the predecessor's formal algebra. The coefficient space is infinite. This is not a word census, not a bounded search, and not a theorem that the monomial vanishes in every physical quotient or at every other D exponent.

The witness `u0 = I` charges four new multiplier monomials, `D3^{-1}`, `-C1 D3^{-1}`, `-Q^{-1} C1 Q D3^{-1}`, and `-Q^2 C1 Q D3^{-1}`, and three new image monomials. They do not remove the residual. No scalar-field minimum and no tape cost are claimed.

## Task and overlap

Base: `17469fff78c22941280f04d39dc5a1faee09c840`. Task: `joint-query-controller`, scope refined. This answers the D-exponent `(0,-1)` question left by open PR #7033. It does not redo the D-exponent-0 obstruction (#7033), the y0 defect (#6951), the declared-family coupling lock (#6945), or the one-edge `C1 Q` row (#6961). The omitted-physical-relation question of #7033 is not taken.

Overlap snapshot on 2026-11-10, via `scripts/find_overlap.py --refresh --all-terms`: local notes at that base (10178 paths, complete inventory), 339 open-PR records fetched at 10:15:04Z, and 7013 discussion records fetched at 10:16:06Z. Requiring both phrases `D exponent (0,-1)` and `owner-indexed` matches only discussion reply 19513867, which asks this question. PR #7033 states the same question with the exponent in backticks, so that literal pair misses its body; the PR was read directly. The search is not a novelty certificate. Closed PR bodies were outside that snapshot.

## Validation

Python 3.12, standard library only. From the repository root:

```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/owner-indexed-d3-inverse-term --check-only
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/owner-indexed-d3-inverse-term
```

Both registered commands passed locally, including the optimized run. Checks are explicit `need` failures, not assertions. The syllable-length-4 replay is a control, not a census of `u0`. No network, native build, or full multiplier replay is used.

## Open next questions

Can a D-exponent `(0,1)` correction of the same sharp index, using two or more banks, make the fresh x1 column zero while keeping `x0 = D1 Q^{-1}` and y0 zero? One homogeneous term on one bank is already blocked for every degree by the monomial gate proved here. The same coefficient shape keeps the boundary at `D3`, and for `u0 = I` the degree-`(1,1)` line properly contains the residual. The first step is to decide whether any D-exponent-0 `u0` makes `R + u0 Δ_+` the zero element, and to charge every monomial of a solution. No such `u0` is solved here.
